- If sentiment is consistently 0.00, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon and underestimates later — adjust forecast slope downward after initial spike.
- If sentiment is >0.00 (even low), model often overreacts to recent highs — cap forecast growth after 3–5 consecutive days of rising prices.
- When true outcome shows sharp downward spike after a peak, model often fails to correct — add a 1–2 day lagged correction to forecast.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows strong mean reversion, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5 days.
- If sentiment is 0.00 and true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, model is underestimating — increase forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment shifts.
- If forecast is rising steadily and true outcome shows sudden drop, model is overconfident — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3 days if sentiment remains 0.00.
- If sentiment is 0.00 and forecast is rising >10% from prior day, model is overestimating — cap forecast at prior day’s value + 1% unless sentiment >0.25.
- If true outcome shows strong upward momentum after a low, model often lags — add 1–2 day lag to forecast peak detection.
- If sentiment is 0.00 and forecast is below true outcome by >3% for 5+ days, model is underestimating — increase forecast by 0.5–1% per day until sentiment changes.
- If forecast is rising and true outcome shows no trend, model is overfitting — reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for next 3 days.
